title: Replication Codebase: Customs aggregation and scarcity pricing drive a trillion-dollar global threatened seafood trade
description:
Clean, reproducible Python analytical and econometric codebase for the study: "Customs aggregation and scarcity pricing drive a trillion-dollar global threatened seafood trade" (submitted to Nature Sustainability).

This repository contains exclusively the 20 sequential Python scripts (01–20) implementing species-to-HS6 conservation concordances, Taxonomic Aggregation Ratio (TAR) and Species Customs Resolution Index (SCRI) audits, 37-year UN Comtrade and 30-year CEPII BACI Dual-IV scarcity pricing regressions, coupled wild-aquaculture bioeconomic differential-equation bifurcation analysis and Pontryagin stochastic optimal control, Comparative Interrupted Time Series and zero-retaining Structural Gravity PPML models, high-dimensional mirror evasion fixed-effects regressions and Stackelberg customs inspection equilibria, live-weight-equivalent marine trophic accounting, non-circular 0–1 binary mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) tariff disaggregation optimization, and bilevel port network interdiction with Monte Carlo Shapley allocation. No raw or derived datasets are distributed; all underlying trade, biological, treaty, and governance records are publicly accessible from institutional repositories.

Author: Sezgin Tunca (Department of Business and Sustainability, University of Southern Denmark, Odense, Denmark; ORCID: 0000-0001-6840-1466).
